why: XLU +3.97 pct to $41.41, the week's leader, through $40.21/$40.66 and the 20D on 52M shares Tuesday, then held three days including the session the 10Y printed 5.364 pct (the fund closed down one cent); the carry gap is still -217bp, the worst in the fund's life, and the 200D ($43.77) has eleven weekly closes under it (wiki/utilities.md; macro/facts.json).

The catalyst was growth, not defense: Google-Constellation 3,590 MW on 15-20 years with $4.3B of CEG-funded uprates, DOE's conditional $4.2B loan to Vistra, Black Hills-Google $1.8B -- all built so the hyperscaler pays, none through the suspended PJM backstop; CEG +15.8, VST +15.3 pct and the nuclear pair is now 10.2 pct of the fund (wiki/utilities.md; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 2).

The formal contradiction (issue filed): utilities-page Ophelia is constructive and set aside her 4.90 pct rule; calendar-page Ophelia says do not buy the dip in anything long-duration before Wednesday 8:30 and utilities need a core print at or below +0.2 pct to hold. This proposal sides with the calendar page for the week horizon and gives the contract leg partial credit (wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.B.1; wiki/economic-calendar.md COUNCIL READ).

Week RF raised 32 -> 42 and MC 38 -> 40: the decoupling from the 10Y is two weeks old and coincides with the biggest contract news of the year; 'a contract-driven decoupling says nothing about what the sector does on the next 10bp without a contract' (wiki/utilities.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 2).
risks: CPI Wed is the direct test: a hot core sends the 10Y through 5.364 pct and the two-week decoupling turns out to have been one news day; falsifier is a close under $40.41 (gap low and 20D) -- the catalyst is being faded; $39.03 voids everything (wiki/utilities.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 5).

The pair ran and wobbled: CEG and VST both put in highs Wednesday and closed 3-4 pct under them with a -5/-6 pct Thursday between; 10 pct of the fund is now a momentum position at 22.4x / 15.5x; Marky wants CEG > $280 and VST > $155 (wiki/utilities.md).

NEE and D (17.0 pct of the fund) are the two parties to a merger Virginia's Lt. Governor formally opposed Oct 7, with the AG asking to reset the review clock; they were the two weakest large caps (+0.7 / +0.5 pct) (wiki/utilities.md).

Bullish falsifier: a close over the 50D $42.01 (not closed above since July) -> $42.42-42.77; a soft CPI with a weekly 10Y close under 5.20 pct narrows the carry gap for the first time since August (wiki/utilities.md).

why: Month arithmetic remains weak (breadth 20, up-volume 29 pct, -5.35 pts vs SPY over a month) and the regime -- a Fed that will hike again, 10Y at a cycle high, 3M bill 4.057 pct and rising -- is the one the sector has lost to for eleven weeks under its 200D (wiki/canary-watch.md; macro/facts.json; wiki/utilities.md).

Against it, the contract template is the one leg of the AI loop that got paid this week and the wires followed in a tidy 2-4 pct band (PPL, SRE, XEL, SO, AEP); Cecil bought DTE at $128.22 and names SRE 14.7x and EXC 13.7x next (wiki/utilities.md; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 2).

Month RF raised 30 -> 38 and MC 45 -> 48: dated items inside the window are NEE Oct 21 (Yahoo, unconfirmed), PCG Oct 22, FOMC Oct 27-28, AEP/NWE Oct 28, PJM's revised backstop filing by Oct 29, XEL/EIX/WEC/DTE Oct 29, D/EXC Oct 30 (wiki/utilities.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: PJM's Oct 29 filing and the governors' bloc demanding accountability on bills: if regulators decide the bilateral deals are themselves the problem, the template breaks; if cost allocation shifts to generators the scarcity premium is the target (wiki/utilities.md WILD CARD).
California: the Oct 8 Eaton Fire continuance hearing has no reported outcome; EIX at 8.5x is 'a name whose next catalyst I cannot read'; PCG reports Oct 22 (wiki/utilities.md).

Falsifier: the 30Y through 5.73 pct and the 10Y through 5.364 pct re-couple the regulated book to the bond; bullish falsifier: more hyperscaler-paid, curtailable deals follow Google's template (wiki/utilities.md RISK SCENARIOS).

extracts.lead_summary: Second up week, and this one had a reason. XLU closed $41.41 (+4.0%), its largest weekly gain in at least four months, and the 10-year closed 4bp lower at 5.24% after printing 5.36% on Wednesday — a 24-year high the sector ignored. The reason was Tuesday: Google signed Constellation for 890 MW of new nuclear uprates on a 20-year contract plus 2,700 MW of existing supply, the DOE offered Vistra up to $4.2B for its own uprates, and Black Hills took a $1.8B Google data-center deal in Wyoming. CEG +15.8%, VST +15.3%, and Vistra enters the top ten. The scarcity trade that FERC put on hold two weeks ago found a route around FERC — bilateral, hyperscaler-paid, outside the auction. The wires rose 2–4% behind it. Last week I said the relief started in the wires and not in CEG; this week CEG led by a mile, and the wires followed. I was early on the leadership call by exactly one week.
